title: Anthropic set its IPO range at $70 to $78 a share, and CNBC says trading starts 19 November. Gemini 4 Carbon is open to all paying developers at $2 and $10 until 30 November. Claude joins Google Meet calls and builds spreadsheets. Businesses can claim ChatGPT profiles. New York and Australia move on AI safety rules. OpenAI can stop research models in 35 seconds. Fireworks AI’s breach widened.
summary: Anthropic launched its IPO roadshow on 10 November, offering 825 million shares at $70 to $78 under the Nasdaq symbol ANT. CNBC says it prices on 18 November and trades on 19 November, at up to about $1.4 trillion fully diluted. Google opened Gemini 4 Carbon to every paying developer at $2 and $10 per million tokens until 30 November, then $4 and $20, while saying Argon still suits most work. Anthropic added Claude Meetings for Google Meet, plus Whiteboards and Sheets, and made Claude Data generally available. OpenAI let businesses claim ChatGPT profiles, see mention counts and, in the US, launch their own agents. New York opened registration for the RAISE Act, which from January requires big labs to report critical incidents within 72 hours. Australia said it will legislate mandatory frontier AI safety rules with a new regulator. OpenAI described Control Room, which stops research model output within 35 seconds of a stop order. Fireworks AI said its breach reached customer datasets and unfinished model weights, and Notion said some AI chat transcripts were exposed.
uncertainty: The IPO share counts and price range are Anthropic’s. The 18 and 19 November dates and the 20 percent retail target are from CNBC’s sources, not Anthropic. The $1.4 trillion valuation is CNBC’s and TechCrunch’s fully diluted figure; Reuters’ first report said up to $1.02 trillion. The $57.75 billion to $64.35 billion raise is TechCrunch’s. Carbon’s rankings and honesty score are Google’s, and the 60.4 percent CursorBench figure is Cursor’s post. Claude Meetings details are TechCrunch’s; Whiteboards, Sheets and Data details are Anthropic’s. The 1.2 billion weekly users figure is OpenAI’s. RAISE Act details are TechCrunch’s. Australia has published no bill, penalties or dates. Control Room’s 35 seconds is OpenAI’s own figure and has not been tested by outsiders. Fireworks and Notion details are as The Hacker News reported their notices.

stories.theme: Anthropic set its IPO range at $70 to $78 a share for 825 million shares, and CNBC says trading starts 19 November
stories.changed: On Tuesday 10 November 2026 Anthropic launched the roadshow for its initial public offering. Its announcement says it is offering 825,000,000 Class A shares, 801,351,354 of them sold by Anthropic and 23,648,646 by existing stockholders, and expects a price between $70 and $78 a share. Anthropic gets no money from the shares the existing stockholders sell. The underwriters get a 30-day option to buy up to 123,750,000 more shares. Anthropic has applied to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT. TechCrunch says the sale would raise $57.75 billion to $64.35 billion. CNBC, citing people familiar with the plans, says Anthropic plans to price on 18 November and start trading on 19 November, and is aiming to give about 20 percent of the shares to retail investors, against the usual 5 to 10 percent. CNBC and TechCrunch say the top of the range values Anthropic at up to about $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis, up from $965 billion in its May funding round. Reuters’ first report on the filing put the target at up to $1.02 trillion, and noted that investors once expected as much as $2 trillion. The registration statement is not yet effective, so no shares can be sold yet.
stories.matters: This is the first time Anthropic itself has put numbers on the IPO, after a week of reports. The range sets the price of the company that sells Claude to many of the businesses reading this.
stories.imply: Do not treat the reported trading date as fixed. It comes from CNBC’s sources, not from Anthropic. Do not quote a single valuation without saying how it was counted. Reuters and CNBC give different figures for the same range.
uses: If your company runs on Claude, note the 18 and 19 November dates in your vendor file. A listed Anthropic will publish quarterly results you can read before renewing a contract.
If you plan to buy shares through a retail broker, check now whether your broker is offering an allocation. CNBC says about 20 percent may go to retail.
Use the official figures from Anthropic’s announcement, 825 million shares at $70 to $78, rather than the numbers that circulated before Tuesday.
stories.example: A finance lead preparing a board note on AI suppliers reads Anthropic’s 10 November announcement. She writes that 825 million shares are offered at $70 to $78, that CNBC reports trading on 19 November, and that the valuation is between $1.02 trillion and $1.4 trillion depending on whose count you use.
stories.audience: Finance teams, investors, and companies that depend on Claude.
stories.watch: The final price on 18 November and whether it lands inside the range. Whether the underwriters use their extra 123,750,000 shares. The first quarterly report after listing. Not a new model.

stories.theme: Gemini 4 Carbon is open to every paying developer at $2 and $10 per million tokens until 30 November, then $4 and $20
stories.changed: On Tuesday 10 November 2026 Google made Gemini 4 Carbon available to developers, businesses and consumers. When Briefing 35 covered its announcement on 28 October, only selected cyber defenders could use it. Carbon is now in the Gemini API for all paying developers in Google AI Studio and in Gemini for business, and it is rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity, the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search. Its introductory price is the same as Gemini 4 Argon, $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Google’s post says that after the introductory period ends on 30 November 2026, the price becomes $4 and $20. Google says Argon remains the right choice for most software engineering and knowledge work, and that Carbon uses more tokens than Argon to explore problems and check its own work. Google says Carbon ranks first on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity’s WANDR and Zapier’s AutomationBench at more than 2 times lower cost per task than the next best outside model. Cursor posted that at high effort Carbon is the top model on CursorBench at 60.4 percent. Google also previewed /swarm in Antigravity, which turns one prompt into a team of agents. On Google’s 375-task agentic honesty test, Carbon passed 92 percent of tasks, against 70 percent for Argon.
stories.matters: A frontier model that was held back for security teams is now something any paying developer can call, at a launch price that doubles in three weeks.
stories.imply: Do not budget at $2 and $10. Plan for $4 and $20 from December. Do not move routine work off Argon just because Carbon tops the charts. Google itself says Argon suits most work, and Carbon spends more tokens per task.
uses: Run your hardest coding or research tasks through Carbon before 30 November, while it costs the same as Argon, and record the token count for each task.
Multiply those token counts by $4 and $20 per million to see what the same work costs in December.
If you use Cursor or Perplexity, try Carbon there first. Both said on X that it is available to their users.
stories.example: A developer at a small agency runs ten tough bug-fix tasks on Carbon in Google AI Studio this week. She logs the tokens each one used, prices them at the December rate of $4 and $20 per million, and keeps Argon as the default for everything else.
stories.audience: Developers and teams choosing a model for hard coding, research and security work.
stories.watch: Independent scores outside Google’s list. Whether Google extends the introductory price past 30 November. How /swarm behaves when it leaves preview.

source.title: Google: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available, 10 November 2026
source.quote: After the introductory period expires on November 30, 2026, the price of $4 per 1M input tokens and $20 per 1M output tokens will apply.

stories.theme: Claude now joins Google Meet calls, builds shared spreadsheets and whiteboards, and Claude Data is generally available
stories.changed: On Tuesday 10 November 2026 Anthropic announced Claude Meetings, Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets, and made Claude Dashboards generally available under the new name Claude Data. TechCrunch says Claude Meetings adds Claude to a video call as a visible participant. It follows the conversation, drafts the plan being discussed, maps a timeline on a whiteboard, answers questions in the meeting chat and pulls figures from connected work apps. The notes, action items and other material it makes are saved in claude.ai afterwards. It is in beta on Team and Enterprise plans and works only with Google Meet at launch. Anthropic’s post says Whiteboards is a shared board that Claude can turn into a timeline with owners and dates, or into a document or deck, and export to Lucid, Miro or Vani by Zoho. Sheets builds spreadsheets with tabs, formulas, formatting and drop-downs, and outlines each edit it makes. Anthropic says Sheets has simple spreadsheet functions for now and can export to .xlsx or CSV. Claude Data adds certified metric definitions, data stories and live sharing, where viewers see approved results without access to the data connectors. On Team plans all three are on by default. On Enterprise plans Whiteboards and Sheets are off by default, and Claude Data turns on by default on 19 November 2026.
stories.matters: Claude is moving from a chat window into the places where teams actually plan: the meeting, the board and the spreadsheet.
stories.imply: Do not assume an AI note-taker in a call is harmless. Claude can pull data from connected apps while people talk. Do not plan around Teams or Zoom yet. Only Google Meet works at launch.
uses: Enterprise admins should decide before 19 November whether Claude Data should switch on by default, in Organization settings, Artifacts.
Try Claude Sheets for a first draft of a tracker or budget, then export to .xlsx if you need full Excel functions.
Tell people at the start of a call when Claude Meetings is listening, and agree which connected apps it may read.
stories.example: A project manager on a Team plan runs a Google Meet kickoff with Claude in the call. By the end, Claude has drafted the plan and a whiteboard timeline with owners and dates. She checks the action items in claude.ai and exports the board to Miro for the wider team.
stories.audience: Team and Enterprise customers of Claude, IT admins, and anyone who runs planning meetings.
stories.watch: Support for Zoom and Microsoft Teams. Whether Sheets gets fuller spreadsheet functions. How admins handle the 19 November default for Claude Data.

source.title: Anthropic: Introducing Claude Whiteboards, Claude Sheets, and Claude Data, 10 November 2026
source.quote: For now, sheets have simple spreadsheet functionality, but we are working on adding more. When you need the full functionality of Excel, you can export your file to .xlsx or CSV, or use Claude for Excel.

stories.theme: Businesses can now claim a ChatGPT profile, see how often they are mentioned, and launch their own agent inside ChatGPT
stories.changed: On Tuesday 10 November 2026 OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT, in beta. Through a new Business Hub, any eligible business where ChatGPT is available can claim its profile, verify it, update key details and add product feeds with prices and availability. OpenAI says ChatGPT has 1.2 billion weekly users. Shopify merchants can connect their store from Business Hub or the Shopify admin. The hub shows aggregated insights, including how many times the business is mentioned, website clicks, and the common topics of conversations where its website is cited. OpenAI says it does not share users’ conversations or Business Agent chats with businesses, and insights appear only above certain thresholds. Eligible ecommerce and online service businesses in the US can also build a Business Agent that answers customers’ questions about their products. That conversation is labeled and kept separate from ChatGPT’s own answers. Businesses can sponsor their agent and use it as the destination for ChatGPT ads, and those placements are labeled. TechCrunch says OpenAI did not explain the verification process. OpenAI’s VP of Monetization, Benji Shomair, told reporters there are multiple verification methods for different businesses and markets.
stories.matters: ChatGPT is building what Google built for search: a profile a business controls, numbers on how it shows up, and a paid way to stand out.
stories.imply: Do not wait for customers to tell you what ChatGPT says about you. Claim the profile and check it. Do not expect conversation details. OpenAI says insights are aggregated only.
uses: Claim your business in Business Hub and correct your hours, products and prices, so ChatGPT answers with current details.
Check the discovery topics each month to see which questions lead people to your website.
If you are a US online shop, test a Business Agent on your top ten customer questions before sponsoring it.
stories.example: The owner of a US online bike-parts shop on Shopify connects the store from her Shopify admin. A week later Business Hub shows how often ChatGPT mentioned the shop and which topics led to clicks, and she adds the missing product sizes to her feed.
stories.audience: Marketing teams, small business owners and online shops.
stories.watch: When Business Agents open outside the US. How verification works in practice. How ChatGPT ads are priced against these profiles. Not a new model.

source.title: OpenAI: Introducing Businesses in ChatGPT, 10 November 2026
source.quote: We’re introducing Businesses in ChatGPT in beta, giving businesses a new way to connect with the 1.2 billion people who use ChatGPT each week.

stories.theme: New York opened registration for its AI safety law, and big frontier labs must sign up by 1 January 2027
stories.changed: On Tuesday 10 November 2026 New York opened a registration portal for the RAISE Act, its AI safety and transparency law. TechCrunch says large frontier AI developers such as Anthropic and OpenAI must register by 1 January 2027, when the law takes effect. The law covers large frontier developers, which it defines as companies with more than $500 million in annual revenue. They must publish safety frameworks on their websites, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours and issue public transparency reports on their models. A new state office, the Office of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity, and Trust, or DIGIT, will enforce it. Penalties can reach $1 million for a first violation and $3 million for later ones. Governor Kathy Hochul also launched the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research at Binghamton University, which will independently evaluate advanced AI systems and work with DIGIT to review companies’ safety frameworks. TechCrunch says Hochul first announced the center in January with $55 million in donations and capital.
stories.matters: From January, the biggest model makers will have to tell a US state about serious safety incidents within 72 hours, and publish how they manage risk.
stories.imply: Do not expect this to apply to your company unless you build frontier models and earn over $500 million a year. Do expect your AI vendors’ safety frameworks and transparency reports to become public documents you can read.
uses: Add a line to vendor reviews asking for each AI supplier’s published safety framework once the law takes effect.
Watch for the first transparency reports from OpenAI and Anthropic, and use them in procurement questions.
If you advise AI companies, check which clients cross the $500 million revenue line.
stories.example: A procurement manager renewing an AI contract in February asks the vendor for its New York safety framework and its latest model transparency report, and files both with the contract.
stories.audience: Legal, compliance and procurement teams, and AI companies operating in New York.
stories.watch: Which companies register by 1 January. The first incident reports DIGIT receives. Whether other states copy the 72-hour rule. Not a new model.

source.title: TechCrunch: OpenAI, Anthropic face new oversight as New York’s AI safety law takes effect, 10 November 2026
source.quote: It mandates that large frontier developers — companies with more than $500 million in annual revenue — have to publish safety frameworks on their websites, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours, and issue public model transparency reports.

stories.theme: Australia will make safety rules mandatory for frontier AI companies, enforced by a new AI safety regulator
stories.changed: On Tuesday 10 November 2026 Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and three ministers announced that Australia will legislate mandatory safety and security protections for frontier AI, through its Australian AI Standards legislation. The rules would apply to all frontier AI companies that want to operate in Australia. The government will propose a new regulator for AI safety, working with the Australian AI Safety Institute, which could impose significant penalties. The release says companies will have to keep security controls across development and deployment, identify and manage serious risks from their models, allow independent evaluation of their models, notify the government of incidents rapidly, publish safety and security frameworks, and respond to updated rules as technology changes. It says the measures follow interim recommendations from the Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence and will give earlier warning of risks from rogue AI agents. The release gives no penalty amounts, deadlines or bill text, and says further details will come after consultation.
stories.matters: Australia joins New York on the same day in requiring incident reports and published safety frameworks from the biggest AI labs. The direction of AI rules is converging.
stories.imply: Do not plan around specific Australian penalties or dates yet. None have been published. Do expect the same few duties, frameworks, independent testing and incident reports, to show up in more countries.
uses: If you operate in Australia, add the AI Standards legislation to your regulatory watch list and look for the consultation.
Compare the six Australian duties with New York’s RAISE Act and the EU AI Act to see what your vendors will have to publish.
Ask frontier AI suppliers whether they already allow independent evaluation of their models.
stories.example: A risk officer at an Australian bank reads the 10 November release. She notes the six duties, flags that no dates or penalties exist yet, and asks the bank’s AI vendors for their current safety frameworks.
stories.audience: Compliance and policy teams in Australia and companies that sell AI there.
stories.watch: The draft bill and its consultation. Which agency becomes the regulator. Penalty amounts. Not a new model.

source.title: Prime Minister of Australia: New Australian AI safety and security protections, 10 November 2026
source.quote: We are announcing today that as part of the Albanese Government’s AI in Australia’s Interests agenda, strong mandatory safety and security protections will be legislated through the AI Standards and apply to all frontier AI companies that wish to operate in Australia.

stories.theme: OpenAI built Control Room, which can stop any research model’s output within 35 seconds of a decision to halt it
stories.changed: OpenAI published a post describing Control Room, a central system that tracks model workloads across its research computers and stops them when safety or security concerns come up. Every research workload that does agentic inference must request a job ID tied to an approved safety case. Before an inference engine answers a request, it asks Control Room whether that job is still allowed to run. Once a job is marked stopped, by a person or by OpenAI’s misalignment monitors, the engine refuses further output for it. OpenAI says it does not trust the research code itself to perform the check. The longest gap between Control Room receiving a stop instruction and output ending is 35 seconds, caused by a caching layer needed for the volume of requests, and OpenAI says it is working to bring that to zero. If Control Room goes down, all inference requests are denied until it recovers. OpenAI says it is already deployed across its research infrastructure, and that its public model-serving stack already had ways to take models down quickly. The 35 seconds does not include the time it takes to notice a problem and decide to act.
stories.matters: It is a concrete, checkable answer to a vague question, whether a lab can actually stop a model mid-run, with a number attached.
stories.imply: Do not read this as covering ChatGPT or the API. It covers OpenAI’s research workloads. Do not read 35 seconds as the time to catch a problem. It is the time after someone decides to stop it.
uses: If your team runs long agent jobs, copy the pattern: every job gets an ID, and the model checks a central list before each step.
Make your own kill switch fail closed, so that if the checker is down, nothing runs.
Ask AI vendors how long it takes them to stop a running agent once they decide to, and how they know.
stories.example: An engineering lead running overnight coding agents reads OpenAI’s post. She adds a job registry that her agents must check before every tool call, and sets it to refuse all calls if the registry is unreachable.
stories.audience: Engineering and security teams running AI agents, and anyone assessing AI lab safety claims.
stories.watch: Whether OpenAI reaches zero lag. Whether outside reviewers test it. Whether other labs publish stop times. Not a new model.

source.title: OpenAI: Control Room, a central system to track and stop model workloads across our research infrastructure
source.quote: The maximum time between the moment when Control Room receives an instruction to stop a job, and the moment when further progress is no longer possible, is 35 seconds.

stories.theme: Fireworks AI’s breach widened to customer datasets, unfinished model weights and some Notion AI chat transcripts
stories.changed: On Monday 9 November 2026 Fireworks AI, which runs AI models for other companies, said its investigation into an incident first reported on 10 October had found more malicious activity. The Hacker News reports that the first notice said only environment variables, including API keys and tokens, were taken from some accounts. The new notice says attackers reached Fireworks’ development machines through an unnamed third-party cloud provider on 23 and 24 October and ran a workload that affected more customer data. For a limited set of accounts that included resource names and descriptions, billing and shipping addresses, invoice and payment history, and a subset of incomplete model weights and datasets. Fireworks says it does not store payment card numbers. It links the attack to a financially motivated group that sells stolen access to language models. Notion said fewer than 1 percent of its workspaces were affected, and that the data included Notion AI chat transcripts used for its Insights feature, mostly not labeled with who wrote them. Notion has turned Insights off and stopped serving open-weight models through Fireworks.
stories.matters: When you use an AI app, your prompts may pass through a model host you never signed with. This is what happens when that hidden supplier is breached.
stories.imply: Do not assume your AI vendor runs its own models. Ask who hosts them. Do not assume a breach notice is final. This one grew a month after the first.
uses: If you are a Fireworks customer, rotate every key and token you stored there and check which datasets and fine-tunes were in affected accounts.
If your workspace used Notion AI, look for Notion’s notice in your workspace and rotate any password or key pasted into Notion AI chats.
Add a question to vendor reviews: which model hosts process our data, and how fast will you tell us about their incidents?
stories.example: An IT manager at a company using Notion AI reads Notion’s update. She checks the workspace for the impact notice, finds staff had pasted API keys into AI chats, and rotates them the same day.
stories.audience: Security teams, IT admins, and companies that build on hosted AI models.
stories.watch: How many Fireworks customers were affected. Whether other apps that use Fireworks report impact. Whether customers leave. Not a new model.

source.title: The Hacker News: Fireworks AI Confirms Wider Breach Affecting Customer Datasets, Model Weights and Notion AI Chats, 10 November 2026
source.quote: Upon analysis of the new data, we discovered that it included Notion AI chat transcripts used for the Insights feature, which for the vast majority of impacted workspaces were unattributable.

CNBC: price 18 Nov, trade 19 Nov, ~20% retail, up to $1.405T fully diluted. TechCrunch: $57.75B–$64.35B. Reuters first: up to $1.02T. Not a new model.

Google, 10 Nov: Gemini 4 Carbon GA for paying API developers and AI Ultra; $2/$10 intro until 30 Nov, then $4/$20. #1 on CursorBench 4.0, WANDR, AutomationBench at >2x lower cost per task (Google). Cursor: 60.4% CursorBench at high. /swarm preview. Honesty 92% vs Argon 70%.

Anthropic, 10 Nov: Claude Meetings (beta, Team/Enterprise, Google Meet only, TechCrunch), Whiteboards and Sheets (beta, paid plans), Claude Data GA. Enterprise: Data on by default 19 Nov. Not a new model.

OpenAI, 10 Nov: Businesses in ChatGPT beta, Business Hub claims, product feeds, aggregated insights; Business Agents for eligible US ecommerce; sponsorable as ChatGPT ads destination. 1.2B weekly users. Not a new model.

TechCrunch, 10 Nov: New York RAISE Act portal open; register by 1 Jan 2027; >$500M revenue developers; safety frameworks, 72-hour incident reports, transparency reports; DIGIT; $1M/$3M penalties. Not a new model.
